summary: Lemongrass corn saute with grilled tofu and quinoa, a 30-minute meal in a bowl with Thai flavors: corn, summer squash, bell pepper and cherry tomatoes stir-fried with lemongrass, ginger, garlic, lime zest and juice, served over quinoa with grilled tofu slabs; vegan, serves 6.
glance: 2 cups, rinsed, 3.5 cups water, about 15 minutes
2 pounds extra-firm in 16 slabs, grilled about 1 minute per side
faq: What is the concept?

A 30-minute meal-in-a-bowl that's light and satisfying, easily customized to your mood or vegetable drawer. This version has Thai flavors (lemongrass, ginger, garlic, lime zest, juice and leaves) but not typical Thai vegetables (corn, cherry tomatoes, summer squash), served over quinoa.
How do I cut corn off the cob neatly?
Rick Bayless's tip: stand a small bowl upside down inside a large bowl, stand the husked ear on the small bowl, and slice along the cob from top to bottom; the larger bowl catches the kernels.
How do I prepare lemongrass?

Remove all but the bottom nearly white portion plus a piece at the end, remove the outer layers so only fairly tender stalk remains, whack it several times with the bottom of a saucepan or the side of a cleaver until flattened, then mince.
Why prep everything first?

The cooking goes fast and you won't have time for chopping: stir-fry the aromatics, then squash and lime zest 1 minute, bell pepper 30 seconds, and corn 2-3 minutes until tender before adding lime juice.
Why rinse the quinoa?
To remove its natural bitter coating; then simmer covered about 15 minutes until tender and the water is absorbed.

summary: Valentine's Day crepes with chocolate ganache and raspberry compote, from a Kavana men's cooking group dinner: Julia Child's blender batter (can be made a day ahead) cooked about 60 seconds and 30 seconds per side, filled with ganache, a quick frozen raspberry compote and whipped cream; serves 4-5.
glance: blend a minute, chill an hour if possible; consistency of quite thin pancake batter
1/4 cup batter per crepe, about 60 seconds, then 30 seconds
8 ounces bittersweet or semi-sweet chocolate melted with about 1/2 cup cream; do not refrigerate
faq: Whose crepe recipe is this?

The batter is classic Julia Child, from Mastering the Art of French Cooking, where she goes into characteristic fine detail on perfecting crepe technique (page 190 in the author's old hardback copy inherited from his mom).
Can I make it ahead?
The batter can be made a day ahead; refrigerate it until ready, ideally at least an hour. Stir in a bit more cold milk if it's too thick.
How do I make the ganache?

Chop the chocolate, add 1/2 cup of heavy cream and melt in the microwave (30 seconds at a time, stirring) or a double boiler, whisking until smooth, adding more cream if needed for a fluffy ganache. Don't refrigerate it.
How do I make the raspberry compote?
Melt frozen raspberries in a small pot, whisking until they turn into a sauce, add sugar and a pinch of salt to taste and simmer until slightly thickened; a little lemon juice or zest is nice.
How do I cook the crepes?

Heat one or two crepe pans or 8-inch non-stick skillets over medium, wipe with oil, pour in 1/4 cup of batter and swirl, cook until just slightly brown but not crisp, about 60 seconds, flip and cook 30 more. Two crepes make a good serving.

summary: Vietnamese lemongrass green beans and tofu: extra-firm tofu fried crispy separately, then garlic, ginger and plenty of lemongrass fried 30 seconds with the green beans until browned (microwaving them first helps), with the tofu and a little soy sauce added back at the end; serves 4 on a weeknight.
glance: 1 pound extra-firm in 1/2-inch cubes, fried separately until crispy and brown
3 cloves garlic, 1 tablespoon ginger, 2 stalks lemongrass, fried about 30 seconds
faq: How do I prepare lemongrass?

Remove the outer layer of each stem, trim away the bottom 1/4 inch and most of the top, leaving only about a 3-inch piece tender enough to sink a fingernail into. Pound it with something heavy to release the flavors (a can of beans works if you don't feel safe using the back edge of a knife), then finely mince it. Do it carefully or you'll end up with woody bits.
Why fry the tofu separately?

The author almost always fries it on its own so it can get serious surface area in a hot pan and develop a crust, then gives it a rest off to the side while the dish cooks and adds it back at the last minute to come back to temperature. Start the tofu first and use the time to prep the rest.
How do I cook the green beans?

Stir-fry, stirring occasionally, until somewhat tender with nice brown spots; if needed add a bit of water and cover a couple of minutes to steam, or pre-microwave 3-4 minutes first, which the author finds a really helpful technique.
How is fish sauce replaced?
Since the author is vegetarian and doesn't cook with fish sauce, a little soy sauce provides background umami.
What can I substitute or add?
Oyster mushrooms instead of green beans, or a bit of finely diced yellow bell pepper for more color. Serve with coconut rice and a lime-dressed salad.

summary: Shiitake congee sous vide, with a ChefSteps vegetarian entree challenge: rice cooked 1 1/2 hours at 90°C with ground dried shiitake and water into a porridge, topped with 45-minute 63°C eggs, pan-fried yuba rolls stuffed with tofu and shiitake, and Chinese pickled greens; serves 4 generously in 2 hours.
glance: Prep 30 min, cook 1 hr 30 min, total 2 hrs
185 grams rice, 40 grams dried shiitake caps, 1 liter water, sous vide at 90°C for 1 1/2 hours
sous vide at 63°C for 45 minutes, or soft-boiled
Vegetarian and kosher; vegan if you omit the egg
faq: What is congee?

A thin, savory rice porridge eaten in one form or another all over Asia, often for breakfast: a blank slate that can be topped with just about anything. This one is flavored with dried shiitake for profound umami intensity.
Do I need sous vide?

No. The author cooked it sous vide mostly as an experiment: you can readily cook congee in a rice cooker, on the stovetop, in a pressure cooker or a slow cooker. In the bag, the shiitake aroma stays very clear, and with more testing the water amount would be consistent.
What is sous vide?

Cooking food sealed in a vacuum or plastic bag in a water bath with precise control of the final internal temperature. ChefSteps' mission is to show it isn't just for professionals, isn't expensive and doesn't have to be scary.
How do I make the yuba rolls crispy?

Fill 12 rectangles of fresh soybean skin (yuba) with 1 tablespoon of tofu and shiitake mixture each, wrap tightly without sealing the ends, and pan-fry as close to serving time as possible until golden brown. Grant Grilly's untested tip: deep fry them two or three times, first at a lower temperature to remove moisture and then higher to crisp.
What was the challenge?
A weekly culinary challenge on the ChefSteps forums, just for fun: a vegetarian entree in any style with at least one component cooked sous vide. The author asked vegetarian readers to join in.

summary: Potato salad with feta cream dressing: small Yukon gold potatoes boiled just tender and halved, tossed with a garlicky dressing of feta whizzed with cream, smoked paprika and lemon, crispy fried capers, gherkins, dill, oregano, parsley and green onions, then chilled; serves 6 as a side.
glance: 3 pounds small Yukon golds, boiled until just tender, halved
4 ounces feta, 3/4 cup cream, garlic, smoked paprika, lemon; a little thicker than sour cream
2 tablespoons fried in olive oil until crispy
faq: Why a feta cream dressing?

The author wanted a potato salad that wouldn't be cowering in the corner, afraid of being bullied by the borekas and boyikos at his wife's family's Sephardic Mother's Day brunch, so instead of mayonnaise or vinaigrette he made an assertive dressing.
How thick should the dressing be?
A little thicker than sour cream, remembering that it will tighten up as it cools, and quite intensely flavored because it dresses a lot of potatoes.
What potatoes should I use?

Tiny Yukon golds so you can just cut them in half, which looks nice. If you can't find small ones, use any waxy potato cut into bite-sized dice. Boil until just tender but definitely not falling apart.
How do I make the capers crispy?
Drain them, dry on paper towels, and fry in the olive oil in a small pan over medium-high heat until crispy and brown, then drain on paper towels.
How do I serve it?
Chill, then toss again and garnish with more feta and parsley, and chive blossoms broken into their tiny purple flowers if you have them.

summary: Indian fry bread tacos: tender Navajo fry bread dough mixed with milk and barely kneaded, rolled to 9 inches and fried at 365°F to medium golden, topped with pinto beans, a poblano, squash and corn saute, cheddar, lettuce, guacamole and salsa; serves 4.
glance: oil 3/4 inch deep at 365°F, one at a time, until medium golden brown
3 cups flour, baking powder, salt, 1 cup milk; knead only a few seconds
faq: What is the history of fry bread?

Navajo fry bread and the Indian tacos made with it originated in Native American internment camps set up by the U.S. government in the 1860s, as a way to use very limited rations. Today they are a proud part of the culture, served at virtually every powwow.
What are they called?
The folks who make and eat them universally call them "Indian tacos"; the author notes that "Native American," though usually the more diplomatic term, is never applied to this dish.
How do I keep fry bread tender?
Don't knead the dough any more than is absolutely necessary to bring it together, and fry it only until lightly golden brown: you aren't looking for a crisp shell.
How do I fry the breads safely?

Bring 3/4 inch of oil to 365°F, divide the dough into 4 balls and roll each to about 9 inches, fry one at a time flipping carefully; they're big enough that flopping one over can cause a dangerous splash, so use a spatula and a spoon.
What can I do with leftover dough?
Fry it up and serve with confectioners' sugar or honey for a treat.
What are rajas?
Roasted, peeled poblano peppers cut into 1/4-inch strips in Mexican cuisine; roast them until blackened and blistered, steam in a covered bowl, and wear rubber gloves to peel and seed them.

summary: King oyster mushrooms with Marcella Hazan's buttery pesto, grilled polenta and white beans: mushrooms sliced 1/8 inch thick lengthwise and seared in olive oil, served on caramelized onion cannellini with crisp grilled polenta squares and a dollop of pesto; serves 4.
glance: 4 large king oyster, sliced 1/8 inch thick lengthwise, a few minutes per side
cook, chill at least 2 hours or overnight, slice 3.5-inch squares no more than 1/2 inch thick, grill
Marcella Hazan's, with 3 tablespoons softened butter
faq: Are French horn mushrooms the same as king oyster?

Yes. The author saw "French Horn Mushrooms" at Whole Foods for $19.99 a pound and confirmed they're the same Pleurotus eryngii as the "King Oyster Mushrooms" at Asian groceries for $6-8 a pound; they're also called king trumpet.
How do I get umami from king oysters?
Slice them thinly and sear them. They brown beautifully, developing a meaty texture that can stand up to a flavorful sauce; the author corrected a Wikipedia article that claimed they were tasteless.
What is Marcella Hazan's pesto method?

She mixes in 3 tablespoons of softened butter after blending the basil, olive oil, nuts, garlic and salt into a paste and stirring in the cheeses by hand. The author says it adds another dimension of smooth sweetness.
How do I keep basil fresh?
Whole Foods sells "living basil" with roots attached in a moist packet; bring it home and store it on the counter in a glass of water until ready to use for maximum flavor.
How do I make grilled polenta?

Cook the cornmeal, pour into a buttered 12 x 12 pan and refrigerate until cool and firmly set (at least 2 hours or the night before), slice into 3.5-inch squares, oil well and cook on a grill pan or skillet until crispy. De la Estancia polenta cooks in a minute.

summary: Blue potato tarts: thin slices of purple potato steamed with rosemary, laid in overlapping rows over a chevre and cream spread on two baked 12 x 4-inch pastry rectangles, baked 10 minutes more and finished with aged balsamic and parsley; makes 10 two-bite appetizer portions.
glance: 30 minutes if the tart dough is already chilling
6 small purple potatoes, sliced 1/16 to 1/8 inch, baked covered about 15 minutes
two 12 x 4-inch rectangles of basic pastry dough baked 10-15 minutes
faq: What potatoes should I use?
A variety that is blue or purple all the way through, to show off the presentation. Other varieties work; it's nice if they're small enough to arrange whole slices on the rectangular tarts.
How do I slice and cook the potatoes?

Slice very evenly and thinly, 1/16 to 1/8 inch, ideally with a mandoline or food processor slicing blade. Toss in a covered baking dish with olive oil, salt, a rosemary sprig and 2 tablespoons of water and bake at 400°F about 15 minutes until fully tender but not falling apart.
How do I make the tart crusts?
Roll basic pastry dough into two 12 x 4-inch rectangles on a lined sheet, form a thin raised edge by hand, prick all over with a fork and bake until golden brown, 10-15 minutes. Cool 10 minutes.
How do I assemble the tarts?

Brush the crusts with olive oil, spread a whisked mixture of cream, chevre, garlic and salt, overlap the potato slices (revealing about 1/8 inch of each), brush with oil and salt, then bake about 10 minutes to heat through. Garnish with aged balsamic and parsley and cut each into five.
What if I have truffle salt?
Use it throughout for an extra dimension of flavor; regular kosher salt is still delicious.

summary: Heirloom tomato tart in an 11-inch tart pan: pastry brushed with olive oil, filled with aged provolone and basil, topped with close-fitting heirloom tomato slices and halved cherry tomatoes, baked about 45 minutes at 400°F (pricking the tomatoes after 10 minutes) and finished with fresh basil; serves 4-6.
glance: 400°F (convection helps) for about 45 minutes, until the crust is golden brown
1 cup grated aged provolone, or any flavorful melting cheese
2 large heirlooms sliced 1/4 inch parallel to the base, plus halved cherry tomatoes
faq: How do I use herbs in the tart?

A useful trick with fresh herbs is to add them twice: once early in the cooking for a deep infused flavor, and again at the very end for bright green notes. With rosemary, mince it finely and only do the first addition.
How do I keep the crust from getting soggy?

The tomatoes release moisture, so the bottom crust won't be perfectly crisp, though it is still delicious. Brushing the crust with olive oil helps; convection helps drive off moisture; if you have time, roast the tomatoes separately and blind-bake the crust.
Why prick the tomatoes?
After about the first ten minutes of baking, prick all of the large tomato slices a few times with a fork (even gently pushing down on them) to aid moisture release without distorting their shape.
How do I slice the tomatoes?
Core them and slice parallel to their base (not vertically), about 1/4 inch thick, skipping the top and bottom slices; fit them as closely together as possible and fill gaps with cherry tomatoes.
How should I serve it?

Cool 10 minutes, top with the remaining basil, flaky salt and pepper, and serve with a green salad for a light meal or in smaller slices as an appetizer. Any flavorful cheese that melts well can replace the provolone.

summary: Persian-Italian eggplant stew, a reimagined fesenjan-e bademjan: eggplant quarters seared in olive oil, then simmered about 10 minutes in a sauce of cumin, cinnamon, cayenne, mosto cotto (saba), honey, red wine vinegar and sunflower butter, garnished with parsley and sumac; serves 4.
glance: 3 medium or 2 large, quartered lengthwise and fried on all sides until golden
2 tablespoons each mosto cotto, honey, red wine vinegar and sunflower butter, with 2 cups water
about 10 minutes until the eggplant is tender and the sauce thickened
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you replace the honey
faq: What is the original dish?
Fesenjan-e bademjan, a Persian dish of eggplant braised in a sauce of walnuts, pomegranate molasses and honey. The author had no pomegranate molasses and can't serve walnuts, so he improvised.
What is mosto cotto?

Also called saba: cooked grape must that would become balsamic vinegar if it were aged. It is fruity, sweet and sour in a way comparable to pomegranate molasses; the author imagined the dish cooked by a Persian traveling on a trade route through Italy in the 10th century.
What replaces the walnuts?
Roasted, unsweetened sunflower seed butter, since the walnuts' main purpose is to thicken and enrich the sauce. Walnut butter or toasted and ground walnuts would also work.
Should I salt and drain the eggplant?
The author doesn't: some feel it's essential to remove bitterness, but to him it just makes them wet so they don't brown well, and he doesn't find them particularly bitter.
How do I make it vegan?
Replace the honey with something like agave nectar.
How should it taste?
A complex mixture of spices, sweet and sour; taste and add more salt, pepper, cayenne or vinegar as needed. The sweet, sour and spiced flavors seem almost medieval.
